tasks.task: Write a month's batch of LinkedIn posts in the client's voice

items.when: Each month, to run notes, interview, drafts, approval and scheduling in a fixed order
Before the new batch, to see which of last month's posts worked and why reach changed
When you have notes, wins, mistakes and opinions and need 8 to 12 posts in a mix of types
When a post needs a stronger first line, to try several opening patterns
Before sending the batch for approval, to fix lines the client would never say

tasks.task: Build a voice profile from the client's own words

items.when: When the samples are voice memos or talks, to turn them into text first
When you have the client's unedited words and need one page every draft can follow
When the client has many documents and wants a guide plus a check of new copy against it
When the client's team needs the profile as one page with before and after lines
When the profile is agreed, to check each later draft against it

tasks.task: Prepare and run a story-mining interview

items.when: Before an interview or voice memo session, to get scenes, numbers and opinions, not generalities
When the expert's judgment is hard to put in words, to draw it out case by case
When you have the facts of a turning point, to map them into a story shape
When the client gives polished answers, to ask the question that gets the real one
When the session is a live call, to record it and get a transcript to write from

tasks.task: Find content pillars and a bank of idea prompts

items.when: When the client posts about everything, to find three to five subjects they can own
When the goal is known, to set pillars, positioning and a posting rhythm they can keep
When the bank runs dry, to get ten prompts the client can answer by voice memo
When the client has old articles, talks or transcripts that hold posts

tasks.task: Fix weak first lines and endings

items.when: When a post or intro is written but the first lines are weak or the ending begs
When you want to see the same idea opened in a different pattern
When the hook sounds like every other post, to fix the machine-made lines

tasks.task: Write an opinion article from the client's notes

items.when: Before drafting, to find the true but unpopular belief behind the idea and who disagrees
When notes, memos or an interview must become a piece under the client's name
When the argument will be attacked, to answer the toughest objections fairly
When the piece needs a title, to compare several honest angles
When the argument is vague, to say the claim plainly and test each step
Before it goes to an outlet, to list every claim that needs a source, ranked by risk

tasks.task: Write a founder story cut to what moves

items.when: Before writing, to lay the true facts out as a call, a struggle and a change
When you have the facts of how they started and need the story shaped and cut
When the story comes from an interview and must sound like the founder telling it
When the story could start in several places, to find the moment with the surprise
When the story lists achievements, to find the one true incident that shows who they are
Before approval, to check the story sounds like the founder and not a profile writer

tasks.task: Write an about page

items.when: When the about page should come from the founder's own account
When you have how and why they started and need a page that sounds like them
When the page opens flat, to compare five headlines with a subhead
When the page is drafted, to fix lines that sound like a template

tasks.task: Rewrite a LinkedIn profile and bio

items.when: Before rewriting, to decide what the client wants to be known for and by whom
When the profile needs a stronger headline, About section and experience lines
When the bio is a dry list, to add one or two sharp, true lines
Before it goes live, to make sure the profile reads like the person

tasks.task: Write a document carousel post

items.when: When one idea should become a carousel script, slide by slide
When the first slide must earn the swipe, to compare openings
When the slides are drafted, to cut filler lines

tasks.task: Build a comment and outreach playbook

items.when: When the client wants the right conversations: who to comment on and how to connect
When a comment should add something new in the client's voice
When replies to comments on the client's own posts need drafting each week
When a comment thread should turn into a first message that sounds like the client

tasks.task: Write X posts and threads in the client's voice

items.when: When you have posts the client wrote, to get new ones that sound the same
When one idea needs an X post and a LinkedIn post that read as written apart
When a long idea or transcript should become a thread where each post stands alone
When the first post is weak, to compare openings
Before scheduling, to catch lines that do not sound like the client

tasks.task: Test the big idea for a book, course or talk series

items.when: At the start, to turn a pile of material into one sentence that can carry the project
When the idea sounds agreeable, to see whether anyone would disagree with it
When the idea holds, to try it as several working titles
When the idea is abstract, to find the one real case that makes a reader care

tasks.task: Write a book proposal and chapter plan

items.when: When an expert with years of posts or talks wants a book, to run the steps in order
When you need the big idea, title options, reader, chapter plan and proposal sections
When the author needs an outline and a writing plan for their stage
When one chapter's material needs a clear order before the plan is fixed

tasks.task: Draft a chapter from the author's notes

items.when: When voice notes and rough ideas must become a chapter in the author's own voice
When the chapter must please experts and newcomers, to try a version that does both
When the chapter is all material and no point
Before the author reads it, to fix what does not sound like them
When the chapter is drafted, to edit and re-check it until it passes

tasks.task: Coach an author through the writing months

items.when: When the author keeps stalling, to set a daily count, a reading plan and a restart rule
Each week, to read the log for days hit, pace and a likely finish date
When the author is stuck at one stage and needs the next steps

tasks.task: Plan a book launch

items.when: When there is a date, to plan the teaser, the preview and launch day
When the author has a list, to plan the launch emails up to the close date
When the book is self-published and needs a price and honest launch wording
When the book needs reviewers and podcasts: a list, pitches and a press kit outline

tasks.task: Edit a draft until it sounds like the named author

items.when: When a draft is right on the facts but does not sound like the author
When there is a written voice profile, to rank where the draft departs from it
When the draft has stock phrases the author would never use

tasks.task: Check a ghostwriting job for honesty and outlet rules

items.when: Before taking a job, and again before a piece goes to a platform, publisher or contest
When the client's team uses AI, to agree what AI drafts and what a person must own
Before the client puts their name on it, to check every fact and number

tasks.task: Write a personal story email or newsletter

items.when: When one true story should become an email, with a read of how it did after
When you want three different drafts from the same story to choose from
Before sending, to compare subject lines from several angles
When the email is drafted, to get cuts, a pacing map and a ship or fix call

tasks.task: Write a talk opening or short speech

items.when: When the client's story should open a talk
When the talk needs one case to carry it from start to request
When the words will be heard, to shape them for the ear with a refrain
When the room wants to laugh, to try a deadpan version built on one true story
When the script is drafted, to fix lines that trip when spoken

tasks.task: Write an annual letter or investor update

items.when: When you have the year's numbers and need principles, metrics and a plain letter
When staff, owners and investors each get a version, to find where they contradict
Before it goes out, to list the toughest questions readers will ask

always.when: When a piece states facts, names or numbers under the client's name, to check each one
Before any draft goes for approval, to catch phrases that read as machine written
Last step before sending, to catch slips with a log of every change

helpers.when: When a long draft needs a structural edit or a final proofread by fresh eyes
When the client needs a full keynote or a speech for an occasion, not only an opening
When an article needs placing in an outlet, or a book needs press
When posts need scheduling, replies and reporting across channels
When a carousel or deck needs designed slides, not only the words
When the founder's content must tie into search, email and a company content plan

gaps: No library item builds a voice profile of one person from their unedited words; the voice guides are made for brands
No library item scores how close a draft is to the author's own samples
No library item writes a book proposal for agents: comparable titles, market, author platform and a query letter
No library item drafts a non-fiction chapter from notes, apart from one imported agent
No library item writes a LinkedIn document carousel for an expert; the carousel writers are for ads
No library item fits an opinion article to an outlet's rules or pitches it to an editor
No library item checks a ghostwritten piece against platform, publisher or contest rules on disclosure and AI use
No library item writes a speaker one-sheet or a bio in three lengths
No library item makes clearly different versions of an annual letter or investor update
